title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: A closing brace is not always the end
summary: A member whose expression body carried on past a lambda lost that continuation: the cut took the first line and left `?: View.GONE` alone in the file.

highlights.title: Expressions that continue past a lambda
highlights.description: The span stops on the lambda closing brace, so the end is not line based and the continuation test was gated on that. A positive test answers now where the span cannot: a line opening on `?:`, `.`, `::` or `else` can only continue what is above it.

highlights.title: The walk stopped allocating
highlights.description: It cut one substring per line it read. A single pass never got slower, but the workspace sweep fell into a slow mode 65 % of the time against 30 % before. Counting over indices puts both back at the same rate.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: A member whose expression body carried on past a lambda lost that continuation, and the remainder no longer compiled. Three such members on a real 6329 source project, all live code.
The expression walk counts brackets over indices instead of cutting a substring per line.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: Found by a new invariant in the removal witness: the seven already there watch what a cut CONTAINS, not one watched what it LEAVES. It compares indentation, chosen because it does not replay the production rule it judges.
